newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks helped by Dow, Dax to record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks helped by Dow, Dax to record close.

text.p: Swiss shares ended at a new closing high on Wednesday, propelled by gains on Wall Street and the German Dax index.
Dealers said buying momentum increased in the second half of the session as U.S. bond and stock markets recovered. Shares firmed despite weakness in Swiss government bond futures.
"There is a feeling that the recent conslidation is over," one share trader said, adding there was ample liquidity in the share market due to the lack of investment alternatives.

News the Swiss government, together with the Swiss National Bank, is proposing to set up a substantial memorial fund, may also have had a positive impact. The fund, to be funded by a revaluation of Swiss gold reserves, follows allegations that Swiss banks were a cache for Nazi wealth in World War Two.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 33.4 points, or 0.74 percent, at 4,547.1 points, topping the previous record close of 4,539.0 points set on February 26.

The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 20.39 points, or 0.71 percent, to 2,890.83. Volume was heavy. One dealer said gains in SMI futures also underpinned cash stocks. March SMI futures rose 35.5 points to 4,552.5. The outlook still was favourable, traders said.

Profit-taking erased some of the initial gains of CS Group, which reported a 1996 net loss of 2.432 billion Swiss francs. News of a larger than expected loss, after an extensive restructuring last year, was largely offset by a positive outlook. CS Group led the actives list, falling 0.25 francs to 158.25 after an early rise to 161.
Dealers said financials were sought initially, but the buying spree later extended to industrials as well.

Swiss Bank Corp jumped six francs or more than two percent, to 290. Union Bank of Switzerland bearers were up 12 francs at 1,340. Major insurers Zurich, Swiss Re and Winterthur were all more than one percent higher.
Share rights on Ciba Specialty Chemicals jumped 1.60 franc to 99.00. Novartis registered shares added nine francs to 1,710. Roche recovered from early weakness, adding 60 francs to 12,320.
Watchmaker SMH and Chemical firm EMS ended lower.
